raw_text:
Here’s a 12‑week, phased programme starting 2026‑06‑01 designed to improve body composition and insulin sensitivity for a 31‑year‑old recreational lifter with PCOS (irregular cycles, sometimes anovulatory), HbA1c 5.8, BMI 28. It prioritises progressive resistance training as first-line therapy, moderates total stress (no crash dieting, no excessive cardio), and builds sustainable habits for glycemic control, strength, and lean mass. The plan includes training, conditioning, recovery, and nutrition guidelines, with week‑by‑week progression.

Overview
- Phases (12 weeks total):
  - Weeks 1–3: Rebuild & Prime (hypertrophy technique, insulin-sensitising volume, aerobic base)
  - Weeks 4–6: Progressive Overload (hypertrophy → strength-endurance)
  - Week 7: Deload & Reset (reduce volume, maintain intensity)
  - Weeks 8–10: Strength & Recomp (higher intensity, moderate volume)
  - Weeks 11–12: Consolidate & Recomp (hybrid strength-hypertrophy, slight density bump)
- Weekly structure: 4 lifting days + 1 low-intensity cardio/active recovery day + 2 full rest days
- Session length: 60–75 minutes
- Conditioning: Low-intensity, low-impact only (Zone 2 or incline walking), optional short tempo/intervals introduced conservatively
- Key metrics: RPE, sleep, menstrual symptoms, morning HR, perceived stress, fasting glucose (if available), body weight/waist, training logs

Global training notes
- Intensity: Use RPE 6–9. Leave 1–3 reps in reserve (RIR) on most sets; push closer (RPE 8–9) on last set of key lifts as phases progress.
- Tempo: Controlled eccentrics (2–3 sec) to improve glucose uptake and technique, faster concentrics.
- Rest: 90–150 sec for compounds; 60–90 sec for accessories; longer (2–3 min) on heavy sets in later phases.
- Progression: Add load when you can complete top-of-range reps with RPE ≤8; else add 1–2 reps or 1 set as specified.
- Warm-up: 5–8 min easy cardio + dynamic mobility (hips, T‑spine, ankles, shoulders) + 2–3 ramp-up sets for first compound.
- Cooldown: 3–5 min easy cardio + diaphragmatic breathing (2–3 minutes).

Exercise key
- Primary compounds: Squat pattern, hinge, horizontal/vertical push, horizontal/vertical pull.
- Accessories: Unilateral lower body, posterior chain, core anti‑extension/rotation, glute med, cuff work.

Nutrition for insulin sensitivity and recovery (no crash dieting)
- Calorie target: Mild deficit only if energy availability is adequate and recovery is good.
  - Start at estimated maintenance: ~14–15 kcal/lb x bodyweight. Hold 2 weeks. If weekly average weight is stable and she prefers fat loss, create a small 10–15% deficit (e.g., −250 to −350 kcal/day). Avoid larger deficits.
- Protein: 0.8–1.0 g per lb goal body weight (or 1.6–2.2 g/kg). Distribute 3–5 meals/day, 25–40 g per meal. Include leucine-rich sources (dairy, eggs, meat, soy).
- Carbs: Center carbs around training (pre/during/post); favor high‑fiber, low‑GI sources. Aim 1.5–2.5 g/kg/day baseline; scale up on hard days. Include 25–35 g fiber/day.
- Fats: 0.3–0.5 g/kg/day minimum; include omega‑3s (2–3 servings fatty fish/wk or 1–2 g EPA/DHA).
- Pre‑workout: 60–120 min prior: 25–45 g carbs + 20–30 g protein. If training early, a small 15–25 g carb + 20 g protein snack is fine.
- Post‑workout: 20–40 g protein + 30–60 g carbs within 1–2 hours.
- Hydration/electrolytes: 30–35 ml/kg water/day; add 300–500 mg sodium pre‑training if prone to low blood pressure/fatigue.
- Supplements (optional; coordinate with her MD if needed):
  - Creatine monohydrate 3–5 g/day
  - Vitamin D3 if deficient
  - Omega‑3 (1–2 g EPA/DHA)
  - Inositol (myo‑/D‑chiro per medical guidance for PCOS)
  - Magnesium glycinate 200–400 mg at night for sleep
- Red flags to avoid: Low energy availability, missed meals, large deficits, >2 high‑intensity cardio sessions/week.

Recovery and stress modulation
- Sleep: 7–9 hours, consistent schedule, dark/cool room.
- Stress: 5–10 minutes/day of breathwork, light outdoor walking.
- Deload week (Week 7): Cut volume ~40–50%, keep intensity moderate to maintain adaptations.
- Menstrual/PCOS considerations: If menses occurs, expect 2–3 days of lower power/coordination; adjust loads −5–10% and extend rest as needed. If anovulatory or long cycles, base adjustments on fatigue/soreness and readiness scores.

12‑Week Plan (start: 2026‑06‑01, Monday)

Phase 1: Rebuild & Prime (Weeks 1–3)
Goal: Establish technique, moderate volume for hypertrophy and insulin sensitivity, build aerobic base without stress excess.

Weekly split (Weeks 1–3)
- Day 1: Lower A (Squat emphasis)
- Day 2: Upper A (Horizontal push/pull)
- Day 3: Rest or gentle walk
- Day 4: Lower B (Hinge/glutes)
- Day 5: Upper B (Vertical push/pull)
- Day 6: Low‑intensity cardio + core
- Day 7: Full rest

Week 1 (Jun 1–7)
- Day 1 Lower A
  - Back squat or safety bar squat 4x6 @ RPE 7, 2-0-1-0 tempo, rest 2 min
  - Split squat (rear‑foot elevated if capable) 3x8/side @ RPE 7
  - Romanian deadlift 3x8 @ RPE 7
  - Leg curl (seated/lying) 3x10 @ RPE 7
  - Standing calf raise 3x12 @ RPE 7
- Day 2 Upper A
  - Flat barbell or DB bench press 4x6 @ RPE 7
  - One‑arm DB row 3x10/side @ RPE 7
  - Incline DB press 3x8 @ RPE 7
  - Chest‑supported rear‑delt fly 3x12 @ RPE 7
  - Cable external rotation 2x15 light, control
- Day 4 Lower B
  - Deadlift (conventional or trap bar) 4x5 @ RPE 7
  - Hip thrust (barbell) 4x8 @ RPE 7
  - Goblet squat 3x10 @ RPE 7
  - Cable pull‑through 2x12 @ RPE 7
  - Plank 3x30–45 sec
- Day 5 Upper B
  - Pull‑up/assisted or lat pulldown 4x6–8 @ RPE 7
  - Overhead press (barbell or DB) 4x6 @ RPE 7
  - Seated cable row 3x10 @ RPE 7
  - Lateral raise 3x12 @ RPE 7
  - Cable face pull 2x15
- Day 6 Conditioning + Core
  - Zone 2 cardio: 25–30 min (incline walk, bike, or elliptical) at conversational pace
  - Pallof press 3x12/side
  - Dead bug 3x8/side slow

Week 2 (Jun 8–14)
- Progress: Add 2.5–5 kg to big lifts if RPE ≤7.5 last week; or add 1–2 reps per set within ranges.
- Same split and exercises; slight volume bump:
  - For primary compounds: 4x7–8 @ RPE 7–8 (squat, bench, deadlift, OHP/pull)
  - Accessories: +1 set on first two accessories per session
- Conditioning: 30–35 min Zone 2; optional 4x20 sec brisk strides within walk (not all‑out).

Week 3 (Jun 15–21)
- Compounds: 5x5 @ RPE 7–8 (squat, bench, deadlift, OHP/pull)
- Accessories: 3–4 sets x 8–12 @ RPE 7–8
- Conditioning: 30–35 min Zone 2 + add 5 min easy cooldown walk.
- Mini‑test: Last set AMRAP to RPE 9 (stop with 1 RIR) on squat and bench to set loads for next phase.

Phase 2: Progressive Overload (Weeks 4–6)
Goal: Increase mechanical tension; push last sets; maintain moderate volume to drive hypertrophy and insulin sensitivity.

Weekly split unchanged.

Week 4 (Jun 22–28)
- Day 1 Lower A
  - Back squat 5x4–6 @ RPE 7–8; last set + drop set 1x8 @ −10% load
  - Split squat 4x8/side @ RPE 8
  - RDL 4x8 @ RPE 8
  - Leg press 3x10 @ RPE 8
  - Seated calf raise 3x12–15
- Day 2 Upper A
  - Bench press 5x4–6 @ RPE 7–8; last set AMRAP to RPE 9 (leave 1 RIR)
  - One‑arm DB row 4x8–10
  - Incline DB press 3x8–10
  - Rear‑delt fly 3x12–15
  - Cable ER 2x15
- Day 4 Lower B
  - Deadlift 5x3–5 @ RPE 7–8
  - Hip thrust 4x8–10
  - Front squat or goblet squat 3x8–10
  - Hamstring curl 3x10–12
  - Side plank 3x30–45 sec/side
- Day 5 Upper B
  - Pull‑up/assisted 5x4–6
  - Overhead press 4x5–6
  - Seated cable row 3x10–12
  - Lateral raise 3x12–15 (2‑1‑1 tempo)
  - Face pull 2x15
- Day 6 Conditioning + Core
  - Zone 2: 30–40 min
  - Anti‑rotation press 3x12/side
  - Farmer carry 4x30–40 m heavy

Week 5 (Jun 29–Jul 5)
- Progress 2.5–5 kg on compounds if last week ≤RPE 8; keep rep ranges.
- Add one set to first accessory on each day.
- Optional density finisher once this week only: 5‑minute EMOM of 5 goblet squats + 5 pushups at easy pace (RPE ≤6).

Week 6 (Jul 6–12)
- Compounds: shift to heavier top sets + back‑off volume
  - Squat: Top set 1x3–5 @ RPE 8, then 3x5 @ −10% load
  - Bench: Top set 1x3–5 @ RPE 8, then 3x5 @ −10%
  - Deadlift: Top set 1x3–4 @ RPE 8, then 3x3–4 @ −10%
  - OHP: 4x4–5 @ RPE 8
- Accessories unchanged at RPE 8.
- Conditioning 30–35 min Zone 2.

Week 7: Deload & Reset (Jul 13–19)
- Reduce sets by ~50%, keep RPE ~6–7, maintain movement patterns.
- Example:
  - Squat 3x4 @ RPE 6
  - Bench 3x4 @ RPE 6
  - Deadlift 3x3 @ RPE 6
  - Accessories: 2 sets each, stop well short of fatigue
- Conditioning: 20–25 min easy Zone 2 only.
- Focus: Sleep, walks, mobility, check nutrition adequacy.
- Reassess loads, joint niggles, motivation. If high fatigue, extend deload by 2–3 days.

Phase 3: Strength & Recomp (Weeks 8–10)
Goal: Raise intensity to drive strength and neuromuscular efficiency while preserving lean mass; sustain insulin sensitivity with accessories and step count. Volume moderate.

Weekly split unchanged.

Week 8 (Jul 20–26)
- Day 1 Lower A
  - Back squat 5x3–4 @ RPE 8
  - Bulgarian split squat 3x8/side @ RPE 8
  - RDL 3x6–8 heavy @ RPE 8–9
  - Leg press 2x10–12
  - Calf raise 3x10–12
- Day 2 Upper A
  - Bench press 5x3–4 @ RPE 8
  - DB row 4x8 heavy
  - Incline DB press 3x6–8
  - Rear‑delt fly 3x12–15
  - Cable ER 2x15
- Day 4 Lower B
  - Deadlift 5x2–3 @ RPE 8
  - Hip thrust 4x6–8 heavy @ RPE 8–9
  - Front squat 3x6–8 @ RPE 8
  - Hamstring curl 3x10–12
  - Side plank 3x40–60 sec/side
- Day 5 Upper B
  - Pull‑up/assisted 5x3–5 @ RPE 8
  - Overhead press 4x3–5 @ RPE 8
  - Seated row 3x8–10
  - Lateral raise 3x12–15
  - Face pull 2x15
- Day 6 Conditioning + Core
  - Zone 2: 30–35 min
  - Carry variations: 4x30–40 m
  - Pallof press 3x12/side

Week 9 (Jul 27–Aug 2)
- Progress 2.5 kg where possible; otherwise add a rep on first two sets.
- Introduce low‑dose tempo/intervals once this week only, optional:
  - 6x30 sec steady fast pace (not sprint) + 90 sec easy on bike/rower; total 18–20 min. Replace Day 6 Zone 2, not in addition.

Week 10 (Aug 3–9)
- Intensify with top singles/doubles at manageable RPE to refine neural drive:
  - Squat: 1x1–2 @ RPE ~8, then 4x3 @ −10–12%
  - Bench: 1x1–2 @ RPE ~8, then 4x3 @ −10–12%
  - Deadlift: 1x1 @ RPE ~8, then 4x2–3 @ −10–12%
  - OHP: 5x3 @ RPE 8
- Accessories: Keep RPE 8; do not increase sets.
- Conditioning: 25–30 min Zone 2 or easy outdoor hike.

Phase 4: Consolidate & Recomp (Weeks 11–12)
Goal: Lock in strength, slightly increase density for hypertrophy and energy expenditure without excessive fatigue. Keep cardio low‑intensity.

Week 11 (Aug 10–16)
- Shift to hypertrophy‑strength hybrid, slightly higher reps, shorter rests (75–90 sec on accessories).
- Day 1 Lower A
  - Back squat 4x5–6 @ RPE 7–8
  - Hack squat or leg press 3x10–12 @ RPE 8
  - RDL 3x8 @ RPE 8
  - Walking lunge 2x12/side
  - Calf raise 3x12–15
- Day 2 Upper A
  - Bench press 4x5–6 @ RPE 7–8
  - DB row 3x10
  - Incline DB press 3x8–10
  - Rear‑delt fly 3x15
  - Triceps pressdown 2x12–15
- Day 4 Lower B
  - Deadlift 4x3–4 @ RPE 8
  - Hip thrust 3x8–10
  - Front squat 3x6–8
  - Hamstring curl 3x10–12
  - Plank 3x45–60 sec
- Day 5 Upper B
  - Pull‑up/assisted 4x5–6
  - Overhead press 4x5
  - Seated row 3x10–12
  - Lateral raise 3x12–15
  - Biceps curl 2x10–12
- Day 6 Conditioning: 30–40 min Zone 2 easy

Week 12 (Aug 17–23)
- Slight density increase by adding a final set on the first accessory of each day or using rest‑pause on last set of accessories (e.g., 10 + 3–4 reps after 20 sec).
- Compounds:
  - Squat 3x5 @ RPE 8; last set AMRAP to RPE 9 (leave 1 RIR)
  - Bench 3x5 @ RPE 8; last set AMRAP RPE 9
  - Deadlift 3x3 @ RPE 8
  - OHP 3x5 @ RPE 8
- Conditioning: 25–30 min Zone 2; easy week overall to finish fresh.

Conditioning guardrails (all weeks)
- Total weekly cardio 60–90 min, almost all Zone 2.
- If resting HR elevated >8–10 bpm for 2 mornings or HRV low, cut cardio volume by 30–50% that week.

Autoregulation and PCOS/HPA considerations
- If sleep <6 hours, unexpected hunger suppression, irritability, or persistent DOMS: reduce sets by 1–2 per exercise that day and skip any finishers.
- If cycle starts: reduce compound loads by 5–10% for 2–3 days; focus on technique and accessories.
- Keep step count moderate (7–10k/day) via easy walks rather than extra sessions.

Optional body comp check-ins
- Every 2 weeks (Weeks 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11): track body weight (weekly average), waist/hip, progress photos, performance trends.
- Aim: 0.25–0.5% bodyweight change per week if in deficit; otherwise, performance and waist reduction are primary markers.

Example day of eating (adjust quantities to targets)
- Breakfast: Greek yogurt + berries + chia + honey; 2 eggs on wholegrain toast
- Pre‑training snack: Banana + whey shake
- Post‑training meal: Chicken, quinoa, roasted veggies, olive oil
- Dinner: Salmon, sweet potato, salad with pumpkin seeds
- Snack: Cottage cheese with cinnamon, apple
- Beverages: Water, unsweetened tea/coffee; limit alcohol

End of Week 12 next steps
- If she wants continued fat loss and recovery is solid: continue hybrid strength-hypertrophy with a 10–15% deficit another 6–8 weeks.
- If performance plateau or fatigue rises: take a 5–7 day deload/maintenance phase, then run a new 8–12 week block.

This program keeps resistance training as the anchor for insulin sensitivity, uses modest conditioning, avoids energy crashes, and builds progressively with an embedded deload to respect HPA axis and PCOS considerations.
